- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak for 3–7 days.
- If model forecast is significantly below recent 5-day average (e.g., <90% of avg), consider mean reversion bias — adjust upward by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture long-term trend reversal; if sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish, reduce forecast slope by 10–20% over next 10 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “+1.00” followed by “-0.00” or “0.00”, model tends to overcorrect; apply a 5–10% downward bias to avoid overcorrection.
- When model forecast is >15% above true outcome for 3 consecutive days, apply a “cooling” rule: reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until price stabilizes.
